subject: [Lavaan 0.6-8 using R4.1.0] How are model parameters and degrees of freedom are counted when performing SEM with only manifest variables?

messages.author: 38c11148480bc3d8
messages.subject: [Lavaan 0.6-8 using R4.1.0] How are model parameters and degrees of freedom are counted when performing SEM with only manifest variables?
parts:
Hi all,
I've started recently a project where I have to perform mediation analysis using only manifest variables. As it goes on, I've come to realize I'm not so sure how model parameters and degrees of freedom are accounted for.

So, to make things simple, I took 5 numeric variables from my dataset and I have started to fit simple models and the result is i'm still confused. I'm not the biggest SEM expert there is, so I'm prepared to be educated, but still, I think I may have noticed some inconsistencies.

As a starter: I suppose we are ok that with 5 variables, I have (5*6)/2 = 15 unique variances/covariances to fit (I hope so, otherwise shoot me in the head already cause i'm so dumb...).

1/ A simple regression.
mod <- 'y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4'

fit <- sem(mod, data=test, estimator="ML")
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)

lavaan 0.6-8 ended normally after 13 iterations

  Estimator                                         ML
  Optimization method                           NLMINB
  Number of model parameters                         5

Model Test User Model:
                                                      
  Test statistic                                 0.000
  Degrees of freedom                                 0

> parameterEstimates(fit)
   lhs op rhs    est    se      z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
1    y  ~  x1  0.433 0.076  5.681  0.000    0.283    0.582
2    y  ~  x2  0.230 0.083  2.790  0.005    0.069    0.392
3    y  ~  x3  0.101 0.078  1.306  0.192   -0.051    0.253
4    y  ~  x4 -0.077 0.066 -1.168  0.243   -0.207    0.052
5    y ~~   y  6.460 0.670  9.644  0.000    5.147    7.772
6   x1 ~~  x1  7.930 0.000     NA     NA    7.930    7.930
7   x1 ~~  x2  3.224 0.000     NA     NA    3.224    3.224
8   x1 ~~  x3  1.645 0.000     NA     NA    1.645    1.645
9   x1 ~~  x4  3.277 0.000     NA     NA    3.277    3.277
10  x2 ~~  x2  7.573 0.000     NA     NA    7.573    7.573
11  x2 ~~  x3  3.539 0.000     NA     NA    3.539    3.539
12  x2 ~~  x4  2.433 0.000     NA     NA    2.433    2.433
13  x3 ~~  x3  7.563 0.000     NA     NA    7.563    7.563
14  x3 ~~  x4  2.258 0.000     NA     NA    2.258    2.258
15  x4 ~~  x4  9.676 0.000     NA     NA    9.676    9.676

So, I don't understand how the summary can say there are 5 model parameters, but there is 0 df (to me, it should be 15-5 = 10). All fit statistics such as RMSEA are at max/min value, so it seems the model is just identified according to lavaan but I think there is room for fitting more complex models than just a simple regression with 5 manifest variables. When looking at the parameterEstimates table, it seems all the covariances between exogenous variables are considered estimates, as well as variances. But estimates are fitted values according to the fitted.values(fit) matrix. Indeed, there are no SE, no test statistics, no CI95%. I've tried to fit the same model using the lm() function from base stat and regressions paremeters are estimated at the same value, so I suppose it's not the estimation that is the issue here (if there is any).

2/ Same model but putting all covariances between exogenous variables within the model formula
mod <- 'y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
 
        x1 ~~ x2 + x3 + x4
        x2 ~~ x3 + x4
        x3 ~~ x4'

lavaan 0.6-8 ended normally after 59 iterations

  Estimator                                         ML
  Optimization method                           NLMINB
  Number of model parameters                        15

Model Test User Model:
                                                      
  Test statistic                                 0.000
  Degrees of freedom                                 0

> parameterEstimates(fit)
   lhs op rhs    est    se      z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
1    y  ~  x1  0.433 0.076  5.681  0.000    0.283    0.582
2    y  ~  x2  0.230 0.083  2.790  0.005    0.069    0.392

10  x3 ~~  x4  2.258 0.649  3.480  0.001    0.986    3.529

15  x4 ~~  x4  9.676 1.003  9.644  0.000    7.709   11.642

So, in terms of parameter estimates, it seems it's the same model than before. So, when I saw those results, I was like "oh ok, by default, lavaan estimates covariances between all possible exogenous variables as model parameters". I've tried to mess with some lavaanOptions to see if I can understand but it was a failure. Also, the variances of those exogenous variables are also considered estimates. The paremeterEstimates table is quite close to the fist one but this time all columns are filled. Number of iterations is not in the same range than before... And, this is the really naive question, but should this model not be a 11 model parameters with 4 dfs (I don't understand why the variances of exogenous variables are considered parameters estimtes)? Also, maybe it's a wrong argument but I can fit a more complex model with more paths.

3/ A convoluted model
mod <- 'y ~ x3 + x4
        x2 ~ x1
        x3 ~ x2 + x1
        x4 ~ x1 + x2 + x3'

lavaan 0.6-8 ended normally after 19 iterations

  Estimator                                         ML
  Optimization method                           NLMINB
  Number of model parameters                        12

Model Test User Model:
                                                      
  Test statistic                                49.355
  Degrees of freedom                                 2

> parameterEstimates(fit)
   lhs op rhs   est    se     z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
1    y  ~  x3 0.253 0.080 3.151  0.002    0.096    0.410
2    y  ~  x4 0.092 0.071 1.295  0.195   -0.047    0.231

5   x3  ~  x1 0.021 0.070 0.303  0.762   -0.115    0.157
6   x4  ~  x1 0.338 0.081 4.189  0.000    0.180    0.496
7   x4  ~  x2 0.093 0.091 1.014  0.311   -0.086    0.271
8   x4  ~  x3 0.182 0.085 2.138  0.032    0.015    0.348
9    y ~~   y 8.422 0.873 9.644  0.000    6.711   10.134
10  x2 ~~  x2 6.262 0.649 9.644  0.000    4.989    7.535
11  x3 ~~  x3 5.906 0.612 9.644  0.000    4.706    7.107
12  x4 ~~  x4 7.933 0.823 9.644  0.000    6.320    9.545
13  x1 ~~  x1 7.930 0.000    NA     NA    7.930    7.930

So, to me this model is indeed a 12 model parameters, but lavaan indicates there are only 2 dfs left. It seems the reason is lavaan considerd the variance of x1 (the only exogenous variable of the model) is a 13th estimate. As for the 1st model, it corresponds to the fitted value of the variance.

4/ Let's go crazy by saturating all the paths
mod <- 'y ~ x3 + x4
        x2 ~ x1
        x3 ~ x2 + x1
        x4 ~ x1 + x2 + x3

        x2 ~~ x3
        x2 ~~ x4
        x3 ~~ x4'
 
> fit <- sem(mod, data=test, estimator="ML")
Warning message:
In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified.
> summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
lavaan 0.6-8 ended normally after 19 iterations

  Estimator                                         ML
  Optimization method                           NLMINB
  Number of model parameters                        15

Model Test User Model:
                                                      
  Test statistic                                    NA
  Degrees of freedom                                -1

The model has 8 regressions paths, 4 residual variances, and 3 of them are correlated. So, there are indeed 15 model parameters, but as per lavaan, the model is underidentified.
> parameterEstimates(fit)
   lhs op rhs   est se  z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
1    y  ~  x3 0.253 NA NA     NA       NA       NA
2    y  ~  x4 0.092 NA NA     NA       NA       NA

7   x4  ~  x2 0.093 NA NA     NA       NA       NA
8   x4  ~  x3 0.170 NA NA     NA       NA       NA

10  x2 ~~  x4 0.029 NA NA     NA       NA       NA
11  x3 ~~  x4 0.070 NA NA     NA       NA       NA

13  x2 ~~  x2 6.262 NA NA     NA       NA       NA
14  x3 ~~  x3 5.909 NA NA     NA       NA       NA
15  x4 ~~  x4 7.934 NA NA     NA       NA       NA
16  x1 ~~  x1 7.930  0 NA     NA     7.93     7.93

Again, the variance of x1, the only exogenous variable of the model is considered an estimate.

5/ Let's fit a 5 model parameters by specyfing constraints on the model formula: no covariances between exogenous variables
mod <- 'y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
        
        x1 ~~ 0*x2 + 0*x3 + 0*x4
        x2 ~~ 0*x3 + 0*x4
        x3 ~~ 0*x4'

lavaan 0.6-8 ended normally after 14 iterations

  Estimator                                         ML
  Optimization method                           NLMINB
  Number of model parameters                         9

Model Test User Model:
                                                      
  Test statistic                               118.287
  Degrees of freedom                                 6

> parameterEstimates(fit)
   lhs op rhs    est    se      z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
1    y  ~  x1  0.433 0.066  6.537  0.000    0.303    0.562
2    y  ~  x2  0.230 0.068  3.402  0.001    0.098    0.363
3    y  ~  x3  0.101 0.068  1.496  0.135   -0.031    0.234
4    y  ~  x4 -0.077 0.060 -1.290  0.197   -0.195    0.040
5   x1 ~~  x2  0.000 0.000     NA     NA    0.000    0.000
6   x1 ~~  x3  0.000 0.000     NA     NA    0.000    0.000
7   x1 ~~  x4  0.000 0.000     NA     NA    0.000    0.000
8   x2 ~~  x3  0.000 0.000     NA     NA    0.000    0.000
9   x2 ~~  x4  0.000 0.000     NA     NA    0.000    0.000
10  x3 ~~  x4  0.000 0.000     NA     NA    0.000    0.000
11   y ~~   y  6.460 0.670  9.644  0.000    5.147    7.772
12  x1 ~~  x1  7.930 0.822  9.644  0.000    6.319    9.542
13  x2 ~~  x2  7.573 0.785  9.644  0.000    6.034    9.112
14  x3 ~~  x3  7.563 0.784  9.644  0.000    6.026    9.100
15  x4 ~~  x4  9.676 1.003  9.644  0.000    7.709   11.642

It's the same model than 1 and 2. Estimates of regression paths are the same. This time : 9 model parameters + 6 dfs = 15. But, should it not be a 5 model parameters?

6/ Let's take the simplest model and specify just one covariance between two exogenous variables
mod <- 'y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
        
        x1 ~~ x2'

fit <- sem(mod, data=test, estimator="ML")
Warning message:
In lav_partable_vnames(FLAT, "ov.x", warn = TRUE) : lavaan WARNING:
    model syntax contains variance/covariance/intercept formulas
    involving (an) exogenous variable(s): [x1 x2]; These variables
    will now be treated as random introducing additional free
    parameters. If you wish to treat those variables as fixed, remove
    these formulas from the model syntax. Otherwise, consider adding
    the fixed.x = FALSE option.
> summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
lavaan 0.6-8 ended normally after 21 iterations

  Estimator                                         ML
  Optimization method                           NLMINB
  Number of model parameters                         8
                                                  
                                                      
Model Test User Model:
                                                      
  Test statistic                                69.501
  Degrees of freedom                                 4

So, when I have added all covariances (second example), no warnings, but If i add just one there is an issue. And now, it's a 8 model parameters with 4 dfs.

7/To conclude, I have fitted a one factor CFA with the 4 Xs variables as indicators and the results were crystal clear to me.

In the end, I can really contemplate the possibility I'm stupid. If so, please educate me, I will be thankful. But at the very least, I think there is maybe something a little bit confusing here.

Kind regards,
Antoine Vanier

parts:
Hi all,
So, I did my homework. Turns out the main issue is the fact that I was so used to fit tons on CFA models with latent variables I became puzzled the moment I had to fit a path analysis.

Anyway, I've found a nice website page about the issue : https://fredclavel.org/2014/05/03/disentangling-degrees-of-freedom-for-sem/ .

I' ve read it and I did hand calculations of df for the tested model and the baseline model of all the examples I have tried above and I figured it out. It's cool, I have learned a lot about df and model parameters count in SEM.
To conclude, you can call me stupid. Sorry for the inconvenience. At the very least, I'm a little less stupid now and for others who are confused with this topic, you can check out the link above.

Have a nice day all.
Antoine Vanier
